title: From cheap tool to premium subscription: When a beloved app's price skyrockets
gist: Legacy consumer apps like Evernote, Plex, Quicken and Inkdrop are sharply raising prices to monetize loyal, long-tenured users rather than chase growth. Bending Spoons' SEC filing shows the Evernote playbook: 200+ pricing/retention experiments, usage-limit paywalls driving 51% of conversions, and ARPU per MAU up 2.5x from 2022 to 2025, turning a years-unprofitable app into a record-profit one.

insights.claim: Bending Spoons acquired Evernote in 2023 for its 200 million accounts and highly tenured base, with average customer tenure of 7.2 years at the time of acquisition.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Shows the acquirer thesis: buy sticky legacy software and monetize switching costs.
insights.quote: At the time of acquisition, the average customer tenure was 7.2 years.

insights.claim: Evernote's top subscription tier now costs more than 3.3 times the most advanced tier in 2023 and 10 times the annual price charged from 2008 to 2016, with some users going from $130 to $250 per year.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Quantifies the scale of price extraction possible from entrenched users.
insights.locator: Earlier this year, Evernote, a note-taking

insights.claim: Evernote's new user registrations fell 23% in 2021, 23% in 2022 and 20% in 2023, then rose 29% in 2024 and 20% in 2025 after the Bending Spoons acquisition, per its SEC filing.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Price hikes coincided with renewed growth, undercutting the assumption that they were a desperation move.

insights.claim: Bending Spoons ran more than 200 experiments on Evernote from 2023 to 2025, testing price points, feature impact on retention and onboarding to calibrate how much change users would tolerate.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Systematic experimentation is the core competency behind Bending Spoons' roll-up model, relevant to its valuation.
insights.quote: we leveraged our proprietary technologies to launch more than 200 experiments

insights.claim: After price increases and product changes, Evernote's average revenue per monthly active user was 2.5 times as high in 2025 as in 2022.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Hard evidence that repricing legacy software can dramatically lift unit economics.
insights.quote: average revenue per monthly active user being 2.5 times as high in 2025 as in 2022
insights.locator: Shortly after the acquisition, Evernote prices

insights.claim: Bending Spoons freed previously paywalled Evernote features but added usage limits, which by 2025 accounted for 51% of all subscription conversions, roughly double 2022 levels of limit-triggered conversions in 2024.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Usage-limit freemium is a more effective conversion lever than feature paywalls.
insights.quote: in 2025, such usage limits accounted for 51 percent of all conversions
insights.locator: Bending Spoons also made some previously

insights.claim: Evernote went from being described as unprofitable for years in July 2023 to reportedly reaching record profitability by November 2024.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Rapid turnaround validates the PE-style acquire-and-reprice strategy for mature apps.

insights.claim: The author argues Evernote's price hikes reflect a deliberate strategy to convert customer loyalty into revenue rather than a misjudgment of users' value.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Loyal user bases with high switching costs are monetizable assets, not fragile ones.
insights.quote: The price hikes weren’t evidence of Bending Spoon undervaluing Evernote’s users but rather of the company seeing an opportunity to turn that loyalty into more revenue.
insights.locator: The price hikes weren’t evidence of

insights.claim: Plex's lifetime pass rose from $75 in 2012 to $250 today, a 525% increase over two hikes since March 2024, which Plex said reflected unsustainable launch pricing.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Lifetime deals are being repriced as companies face recurring costs, eroding the lifetime-license model.

insights.claim: Individual plans for Quicken, Robokiller and Inkdrop have each doubled in price in recent years.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Price doubling is a broad trend across consumer software, not an isolated case.
insights.locator: That’s just one example of many

insights.claim: Inkdrop's developer doubled prices to $10 per month in 2024 to deliberately serve a few thousand devoted customers rather than chase more than 10,000 broader users.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Niche indie software is choosing high-ARPU small bases over growth.
insights.quote: I’d prefer to have a few thousand customers who really like my app rather than >10k broader customers.

insights.claim: Mature apps face a structural squeeze: loyal users expect unchanged software at unchanged prices, while stagnant growth clashes with inflation, shareholder expectations and the cost of continued development.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Explains why price hikes recur across mature software and streaming businesses.
insights.quote: stagnant growth doesn’t mix well with inflation or stockholder expectations

insights.claim: The author suggests developers could use grandfathered pricing, more tiers including a cheaper AI-free tier, or add-on bundles for power users instead of across-the-board hikes.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Signals consumer pushback against AI-bundled price increases and demand for tiered segmentation.
insights.quote: A wider range of subscription options, including a cheaper, AI-free tier
